chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Usman ibn Isa, from Abu Zahra, from Umm al-Hasan, who said:

The Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) passed by me and said: 'What are you doing, O Umm al-Hasan?' I said, 'I am spinning.' He said: 'Indeed, it is the most permissible of earnings, or from the most permissible of earnings.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about spinning yarn as a source of income?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this narration from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) to Umm al-Hasan underscores the dignity of manual labor, specifically spinning, as a model of honest sustenance. In Shia scholarly tradition, this highlights the virtue of self-reliance and the prohibition of idleness, framing everyday work as an act of worship when performed with integrity. The Imam’s endorsement serves as a practical guideline for Muslims to find spiritual merit in simple, lawful trades.
